content.comment_body: Hello, I am programming in Ladder and noticed several up/down counters in my project. However, one of them never resets. This feels like a major issue in Ladder, because after converting the program to Function Block Diagram, the counter behaves correctly. Another problem is that after converting to FBD, all blocks are positioned very close together, making it difficult to read. My PLC is: [product_name] [article_no]. Software: [product_name] [version_no]. Thanks for any help.
Could you upload your program? Screenshots don't clearly show the issue.
I've uploaded my program. C055 never resets. Please turn I1 and I4 on, and observe T016 and M3. The LCD displays some information, and after reviewing group 4, the problem appears.

[product_name] [version_no] sometimes has trouble converting between FBD and Ladder. I removed and then reinserted the flag M3 at the counter reset point in your Ladder program, and now the counter resets. The attachment includes the revised program and a video showing the simulation.
It works now, thank you! But could you explain exactly what was changed in the program? It looks the same as before, but functions differently. All the objects appear unchanged. Feels like magic!
Please refer to the next video for further details.

I applied this solution to my own program as you described and it works now. Thank you very much! I was previously converting the original Ladder file to FBD in order to solve the issue. Your advice was helpful. I feel [product_name] works better with FBD, and Ladder is just an alternative. For future projects, do you think it’s better to use FBD from the start? Thanks again.
Hello [user_name], thank you for your positive feedback. I agree—personally, I only write programs in FBD, as I do not prefer Ladder.

analysis.insight_summary: Users noticed inconsistencies in [product_name] when programming up/down counters: a counter failed to reset in Ladder view but functioned after converting to Function Block Diagram or by modifying/resetting specific elements. Schematic readability also diminished after conversion, with blocks becoming crowded together. The issue centers on differences in logic handling and user interface between Ladder and FBD modes in the software.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect counters to behave consistently in both Ladder and FBD views, experience a seamless transition between program types, and maintain readable schematics after conversion.
